title: Feature-level throttles and response morphing for graceful degradation
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Background: During regional capacity contention we currently apply coarse-grained request admission and model-level fallbacks. This causes two problems: 1) user-visible features (tool-calls, structured outputs, long-context completions) are all degraded together even when only a subset cause the majority of extra work; 2) operators lack fine control to preserve critical features for high-value customers while shedding expensive features for lower tiers.

Goal: Implement a feature-level throttling layer plus an adapter that "morphs" responses when a feature is throttled. This should allow the runtime to: (a) granularly admit or reject feature flags per-request (e.g., tool-calling, function response streaming, long completion window, reranking), (b) when a feature is rejected, return an informative, compact degraded response rather than a generic 503, and (c) integrate with existing admission and circuit-breaker systems so policies respect tenant quotas and regional failover rules.

Proposed design:
1) Feature Fingerprint & Budgeting: extend request envelope with a feature list and estimated cost weights (simple integer tokens). Admission controller consumes these and decrements a per-tenant, per-region feature-budget token bucket. Budgets are configurable by priority band.

2) Progressive Fidelity Map: maintain a map that defines an ordered set of degradations per feature. Example for completion: [full-context, truncated-context, summary-only, placeholder]. For tool-calls: [execute, simulate (return predicted call args), annotate-unavailable]. Map is part of release config and can vary per tenant.

3) Response Morphing Adapter: when admission denies a requested feature, runtime invokes the morphing adapter which synthesizes a compact replacement response conforming to the feature contract (e.g., short summary instead of long completion, simulated tool-output, structured error with suggested retry/backoff). Morphs must be deterministic and labelled with a policy code so clients can detect degraded responses.

4) Circuit-breaker & Retry tokens: integrate with circuit breakers so morphing can be used as a graceful fallback instead of tripping the breaker. We add a short-lived retry token header that clients can use to request a subsequent higher-fidelity attempt if capacity recovers.

5) Observability: emit events for feature-denied, morph-applied, retry-token-issued, and morph-failures. Add metrics: feature_denied_rate, morph_applied_rate, morph_success_ratio, p99_latency_by_feature_state.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- Estimating feature cost requires heuristics; initial implementation will use static weights derived from offline profiling (token-rate, kv-cache hits, model variant cost). We accept some misclassification initially.
- Morphing adapter must be extremely small and fast (single-model distillation or template-based) to avoid becoming a new latency hotspot.

Acceptance criteria: (see acceptance_criteria field below)

Implementation plan (high level):
- Phase 1 (spike): add feature list to request envelope and per-tenant feature token buckets. Add profiling job to produce default cost weights. (2 wks)
- Phase 2 (core): implement admission checks and Progressive Fidelity Map evaluation. Add morphing adapter with template-based morphs for top 3 features: long completion, tool-calls, streaming. (3 wks)
- Phase 3 (integration): wire into circuit-breakers, add retry-token header, logging, and dashboard panels. Canary rollout in single region. (2 wks)
- Phase 4 (multi-region): verify behavior for cross-region failover and ensure morphing respects regional policies. Full rollout. (1 wk)

Extra notes: We will expose a simple API for customers to configure their fidelity maps and feature budgets via Console in a later PR (post-v1).
acceptance_criteria: Feature flags can be supplied in the request envelope and are honored by admission controller in canary region
When a requested feature is denied, the runtime returns a morph response that conforms to the feature contract and includes a morph_policy metadata code
During a synthetic overload test (500% baseline RPS spike) P99 latency for P0 routes improves by at least 30% compared to baseline without feature throttles
Morph-applied rate and morph_success_ratio are visible in Console and tracked by rollout dashboard
No customer-facing 5xx from morphing adapter during canary (morph_failure_rate < 0.1%)
Retry-token header is issued for at least 80% of denied feature cases where retry path exists
monitoring: Dashboards: feature_denied_rate (per-tenant, per-region), morph_applied_rate, morph_success_ratio, p50/p95/p99 latency broken out by feature_state (full|morphed). Alerts: page on p99(latency) regression > 15% for P0 routes during canary; warn when feature_denied_rate for a top-tier customer > 1% sustained for 5m.
rollout_plan: Start with internal canary in us-west1 (5% traffic) -> expand to 25% after 48h if no regressions -> enable retry-token experimentation for SDK clients -> full region rollout -> opt-in for multi-region behavior. Feature toggle and kill switch available via Console. Use incremental config pushes for fidelity maps so we can rollback easily.
risks: Incorrect cost weights may over-deny features, causing customer-visible regressions. Morph adapter bugs could leak inconsistent schema. Risk mitigation: conservative default budgets, early canary with synthetic traffic and real-user shadow testing, schema validation for all morph outputs.
